subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept of the skill, What an Error Boundary Catches, Granularity, Pairing with Suspense, Next.js App Router Conventions, Reporting Caught Errors, Common Anti-Patterns, Verification) and the Understanding fields.

cases.scenario: A component has a button whose onClick does `await saveForm()`, which can reject. The team wrapped the page in an error boundary and is confused that a save failure shows an uncaught error in the console and never renders the fallback.
cases.context: The save logic lives entirely inside the click handler; the boundary is an ancestor in the tree.
cases.question: How should the agent fix this?
expected_flags: Event-handler/async errors run outside React's call stack — the boundary cannot catch them directly
Catch the rejection locally with try/catch in the handler
Surface the error into React state via setState(error)
Re-throw during the next render (if (error) throw error) so the boundary catches it
expected_fix_hints: Add local try/catch + setError in the handler
Add `if (error) throw error` in the render path to route it into the boundary
absent_signals: Do not claim the boundary will catch the async error as-is
Do not just wrap a higher-level component in another boundary

cases.scenario: A dashboard renders 8 independent widgets, each fetching its own data. One widget's malformed data throws during render, and the entire dashboard goes blank with a generic 'Something went wrong' page.
cases.context: There is a single app-root error boundary and nothing finer-grained.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the boundaries?
expected_flags: Place boundaries by failure-blast-radius — wrap each widget in its own feature-level boundary
One widget's failure should show that widget's fallback, not blank the whole dashboard
Keep the app-root boundary as a last-resort backstop, layered under route and feature boundaries
Each fallback should be meaningful at its scope (per-widget retry UI)
expected_fix_hints: Add per-widget error boundaries around each data-loading component
absent_signals: Do not rely on a single app-root boundary alone
Do not let one widget's error replace the whole page

cases.scenario: An error boundary renders a friendly 'Something went wrong' fallback but its componentDidCatch only does `console.log(error)`. In production, users hit the fallback regularly and the team has no idea why.
cases.context: There is an error-tracking service (Sentry) available but the boundary doesn't use it.
cases.question: What should the agent change?
expected_flags: A caught error is still an error — a boundary that doesn't report externally is silent UI degradation
Wire onError / componentDidCatch to external observability (Sentry or equivalent)
Include info.componentStack for diagnosis (distinct from the JS stack trace)
The fallback is the user-facing recovery and the report is the developer-facing alarm
expected_fix_hints: Call Sentry.captureException(error, { contexts: { react: { componentStack: info.componentStack } } }) in componentDidCatch
Replace console.log with a real report-to-observability call
absent_signals: Do not leave the boundary swallowing errors with only a console.log
Do not treat the fallback alone as a complete solution

cases.scenario: A team wants a data section that shows a skeleton while loading and an error UI if the fetch fails. They put a single component that tries to handle both loading and error states with try/catch around the suspense-throwing read.
cases.context: They are using Suspense for data fetching and want failure to replace the whole section.
cases.question: How should the agent structure the boundaries?
expected_flags: Error boundaries catch thrown Errors; Suspense catches thrown Promises — they must be distinct components
Nest ErrorBoundary outside Suspense so a failed fetch replaces the whole group including the loading state
Do not try to catch a suspended Promise with try/catch
Wire reset (resetKeys / resetErrorBoundary) so retry re-attempts the failed async render
expected_fix_hints: Wrap <Suspense> inside an <ErrorBoundary> for the common single-failure-surface case
Add resetKeys tied to the query inputs for retry
absent_signals: Do not combine loading and error handling in one try/catch
Do not place the error boundary inside the Suspense slot for the common case

cases.scenario: In a Next.js App Router app, an error thrown in `app/layout.tsx` (the root layout) is not being caught by `app/dashboard/error.tsx`, and the team added more nested error.tsx files trying to catch it.
cases.context: The app uses route-segment error.tsx files but has no global-error.tsx.
cases.question: How should the agent explain and fix this?
expected_flags: error.tsx only catches errors from its descendant tree, not its sibling/parent layout
An error in the root layout escapes every error.tsx and only global-error.tsx can catch it
Add app/global-error.tsx as the app-root backstop
error.tsx must be a Client Component (uses state for the reset action)
expected_fix_hints: Create app/global-error.tsx to catch root-layout errors
Stop adding nested error.tsx files for a parent-layout failure
absent_signals: Do not expect a segment error.tsx to catch its parent layout's error
Do not keep nesting more error.tsx to fix a root-layout throw

cases.scenario: A PM asks the error-boundary owner to design the API's 500-response JSON envelope and to set up the Sentry SDK initialization, sampling, and alerting dashboards.
cases.context: The team conflates 'error handling' across the whole stack with React error boundaries.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: The backend 500 error envelope is out of scope — that is api-design
Sentry SDK setup, sampling, and dashboards are out of scope — that is error-tracking
Offer the in-scope part: the React boundary that catches render failures and reports caught errors into the SDK
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand the wire format to api-design and the SDK/observability setup to error-tracking
Provide the in-tree boundary + onError reporting hook
absent_signals: Do not design the backend error response contract
Do not configure the Sentry SDK and dashboards

cases.scenario: A developer tries to write an error boundary as a function component using a hypothetical useErrorBoundary hook and a try/catch around the JSX, and it never catches descendant render errors.
cases.context: They are on React 19 and prefer function components and hooks everywhere.
cases.question: What should the agent advise?
expected_flags: As of React 19, error boundaries must be class components — there is no useErrorBoundary hook
getDerivedStateFromError / componentDidCatch have no hooks equivalent
try/catch around JSX does not catch a descendant's render throw
Use a class boundary or the react-error-boundary library
expected_fix_hints: Or use the react-error-boundary library for reset and FallbackComponent support
absent_signals: Do not claim a function component can be an error boundary
Do not rely on try/catch around JSX to catch render errors
